title: Run a monotonic user timer
goal: Demonstrate a finite user timer and actual runtime limit.
challenge: Run delayed finite user work without account/linger changes. Prove identity/result and configured loaded limits, then an actual timeout. Explain why retained one-shot state is not a periodic pattern.

steps.command: test "$(systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5.service -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test "$(systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5.timer -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test "$(systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5-timeout.service -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test ! -e "$HOME/ll-s5" && mkdir "$HOME/ll-s5"

steps.explanation: Delay3seconds from activation; retain state for inspection.

steps.command: end=$((SECONDS+10)); until test -s "$HOME/ll-s5/report.txt"; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; cat "$HOME/ll-s5/report.txt"; systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5.service -p LoadState -p Type -p Result -p ExecMainStatus -p RuntimeMaxUSec -p MemoryMax -p TasksMax

systemd-run --user --property=Type=exec --unit=ll-s5-timeout --property=RuntimeMaxSec=2s --property=MemoryMax=64M --property=TasksMax=16 /usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 10s /usr/bin/sleep 20; end=$((SECONDS+12)); until test "$(systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5-timeout.service -p ActiveState --value)" = failed; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$end" || break; sleep 1; done; systemctl --no-pager --user show ll-s5-timeout.service -p LoadState -p Type -p Result -p RuntimeMaxUSec -p MemoryMax -p TasksMax -p MainPID
steps.explanation: Exercise2-second limit with independent10-second safety timeout.

hints: Monotonic delay needs no clock change.
RemainAfterExit retains this single-fire result, not repeating service behavior.
RuntimeMax does not limit Type=oneshot. These exercises explicitly set Type=exec; systemd-run otherwise defaults to Type=simple.
review: Actual timeout with configured2s and no child.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 107.2 partial cron/systemd timers; 105.2/108.2 reinforcement; self-reviewed, unscored. No at or full objective coverage.
